results.content:
Context.dev is the strongest fit here if your app needs web scraping AND company context such as brand profiles, logos, fonts, structured extraction, product data, screenshots, classification, and other enrichment through the same API. Its current API also covers crawling, search, document parsing, batches, and monitors, which makes replacing it harder once several of those features are inside your product.

If you mainly want to search, scrape, crawl, monitor, and feed clean web content into an AI agent, Firecrawl is the alternative I would test first. Its product is heavily focused on web context for developers and agents, while the recurring free allowance also makes it easier to keep testing without immediately taking on another subscription. [...] Context.dev is worth paying for when replacing that maintenance gives you more value than the subscription costs. The Developer plan is especially reasonable for a real product using several of its APIs, because $25 per month is not difficult to justify if it prevents even a small amount of recurring engineering work.

Do not buy it just because the feature list looks impressive. If you only need web scraping, Firecrawl is the Context.dev alternative I would test first; if you need web scraping plus brand intelligence, monitoring, structured extraction, and enrichment inside the same workflow, Context.dev becomes much harder to replace with one cheaper tool. [...] The best Context.dev alternatives and the final verdict The final section narrows the field to alternatives that genuinely solve a similar problem, including Firecrawl for AI-focused web data, Apify for prebuilt scraping and automation tools, and ScrapingBee for a more traditional managed scraping API. You’ll also get the straight recommendation: who should buy now, who should pick a cheaper or more specialized option, and who should keep using Context.dev instead of switching just for the sake of switching.

What is the best Browse AI alternative?

Context.dev is a Browse AI alternative for teams that want web data through an API instead of a no-code robot builder. You send any URL and get Markdown, HTML, a screenshot, or JSON against your schema back, for 1 credit per page with JavaScript rendering and anti-bot handling included, on as many sites as you need. If non-technical teammates will build and maintain the scrapers themselves, Browse AI is the better fit.

How much does a page cost on Browse AI compared with Context.dev? [...] When is Browse AI the better choice?

Choose Browse AI when people without engineering support will build and own the scrapers, when one of its 250+ prebuilt robots covers your site, or when you want its team to run the pipeline under the Premium plan’s 98% data-accuracy SLA. It also has native Google Sheets and Airtable sync and change alerts with screenshot diffs. Context.dev is an API with no visual robot builder.

Can Context.dev scrape pages behind a login?

Yes, on paid plans. Browser profiles let you sign in once with a username and password and reuse the saved session for authenticated scraping. Logins that require MFA or a CAPTCHA are not supported. results.title: Firecrawl vs Context.dev | Choose Firecrawl as a Context.dev Alternative
results.content: The core difference is focus. Context.dev is a web intelligence platform built around brand data - logos, colors, fonts, and company metadata - with web scraping as a supporting capability. Firecrawl is built exclusively for web scraping and data extraction at scale: its /search endpoint finds pages and returns scraped content in one call, its /interact endpoint clicks and fills forms before scraping, its /crawl endpoint indexes entire sites for RAG pipelines, and its /scrape branding format extracts colors, fonts, typography, and visual identity from any URL. Context.dev has no web search endpoint - it requires a known URL to scrape. If your primary need is company firmographics and metadata enrichment, Context.dev serves that well. If you need search-and-scrape in one call, browser [...] Firecrawl is purpose-built for AI pipelines. It returns clean markdown ready for chunking and embedding, with structured data extraction via JSON Schema, brand identity extraction via /scrape branding format, crawl-to-index workflows, and an interact endpoint for dynamic pages. Context.dev supports web scraping and AI extraction, but the platform is designed primarily around brand intelligence and enrichment rather than RAG or agent-building workflows. [...] Yes. Firecrawl is fully open source under the AGPL-3.0 license and can be self-hosted for complete control over your data, compliance, and infrastructure. Context.dev is a proprietary platform with no self-hosting option. For teams with data residency requirements, regulated environments, or a preference for open-source tooling, Firecrawl's self-hosted deployment is a meaningful advantage.

### Context.dev: The Unified Web Context API

Context.dev is engineered specifically as a next-generation Web Context API, unifying Markdown scraping, schema-validated extraction, and real-time brand intelligence under a single developer key. By setting simple boolean flags like `sharedParams.mainContentOnly: true`, it automatically strips header, footer, and sidebar noise without prompt tuning.
